title: Learning When to Stop: Prefix-Optimal Dynamic Diffusion Policies for Continuous Control

paper.title: Learning When to Stop: Prefix-Optimal Dynamic Diffusion Policies for Continuous Control
paper.abstract:
Abstract Diffusion policies have emerged as a powerful policy class for continuous control, but their iterative denoising process remains the primary computational bottleneck. Optimizing the computational effort spent per action is critical for improving the practical adoption of diffusion policies, allowing them to allocate more iterations only when the task demands it. To this end, we propose POGP (Prefix-Optimal Generative Policies), which learns a prefix value function (PVF) at every intermediate denoising step via a Bellman-style recursion over the chain.
The PVF provides both an auxiliary optimization target that shapes intermediate outputs into high-quality actions and a test-time stopping criterion that halts denoising when further iterations are not expected to yield meaningful improvement.
Through extensive experiments on four MuJoCo environments against 12 baselines, we demonstrate that POGP reduces the required denoising iterations by approximately 2.7 × 2.7\times while retaining near-full performance. Furthermore, compared to current state-of-the-art dynamic diffusion baselines, we show that prefix training improves final task performance by approximately 3.5%, suggesting that supervising intermediate denoising steps acts as a beneficial auxiliary objective beyond its role in enabling early stopping. sections.heading: 1 Introduction
sections.text: Diffusion policies for continuous control generate actions through an iterative denoising chain, typically requiring K K sequential neural network evaluations per action ( Ho et al., 2020 ; Chi et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2022 ) . Running all K K iterations of the diffusion process is the primary computational bottleneck of diffusion policies as every action incurs the same computational cost regardless of the task’s difficulty. In practice, however, many actions taken by an embodied system along some trajectory are routine and well-determined after only a few denoising steps, while others, such as contact-rich transitions, disturbance recovery, or mode switches strongly benefit from extended refinement steps. For example, consider an embodied agent perturbed by some external force. When the disturbance is applied to the system, the policy benefits from additional refinement steps to improve the system’s overall behavior while saving compute at other times, which is especially important for local and edge deployments on real robot hardware. Current diffusion policy frameworks ( Ren et al., 2024 ; Ma et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2024 ; Hansen-Estruch et al., 2023 ) do not distinguish between these cases, spending compute uniformly across the trajectory. Recent approaches leveraging diffusion policies ( Yu et al., 2025 ) address this issue by estimating the number of iterations needed in order to reach a sufficiently performant action. However, because this adapter is independent of the policy, the intermediate denoising steps are never optimized to be executable as the model is only trained on the full diffusion process. We take a different approach by jointly training a prefix value function (PVF) alongside the diffusion policy itself, which both improves intermediate action quality as an auxiliary objective and provides a natural per-step stopping signal at test time. In this work, we propose a novel approach for dynamic diffusion – Prefix-Optimal Generative Policies (POGP) – that leverages a learned prefix value function (PVF) to assess when diffusion iterations can be stopped early while improving the quality of internal diffusion iterations . POGP trains a PVF V t ​ ( s , a t ) V_{t}(s,a_{t}) for each intermediate action a t a_{t} in the K K -step diffusion chain a K → a 0 a_{K}\to a_{0} that intuitively measures how valuable it would be to execute action a t a_{t} at step t t . During training, the PVF is trained to estimate an action’s value by completing all K K diffusion steps, co-evolving as an optimization target for the diffusion step itself. Crucially, rather than regressing each V t V_{t} independently against the final action’s Q-value, which would require expensive full-chain rollouts per step, we derive a Bellman recursion over the denoising chain that propagates value information backwards through refinement steps, enabling efficient single-chain training with stable TD targets. Intuitively, the PVF serves a dual purpose: 1) it improves the quality of the intermediate policy actions a t a_{t} ; and 2) provides a metric for stopping the diffusion process early in order to save time and compute budget. We demonstrate that, across four MuJoCo tasks and 12 baselines, POGP achieves an IQM of 0.942 0.942 with a 95 % 95\% confidence interval ( Agarwal et al., 2022 ) , retains ≥ 97.8 % \geq 97.8\% of its full-diffusion process task performance at less than half the computation cost and outperforms current state-of-the-art baselines by ≈ 4.6 % \approx 4.6\% . In summary, POGP proposes the following contributions: • a prefix value function trained via TD bootstrapping alongside the diffusion model over the denoising chain, ultimately improving the quality of the intermediate steps; • a principled early stopping rule derived from prefix value differences across consecutive diffusion steps, leveraged to stop the diffusion policy early if the value of future steps is predicted to be minimal; and • empirical evidence that prefix training improves full-chain performance by up to 4.6 % 4.6\% while enabling ≈ 2.7 × \approx 2.7\times compute savings, on average.

sections.heading: Diffusion Policies for Control.
sections.text: Diffusion-based policies have emerged as a powerful class of decision models for continuous control and robot learning because they can represent complex, multimodal action distributions that are difficult for unimodal actors to capture. Prior work includes action-diffusion policies for manipulation ( Chi et al., 2024 ) , diffusion-based trajectory planning ( Janner et al., 2022 ) , and diffusion-parameterized reinforcement learning methods such as Diffusion-QL ( Wang et al., 2022 ) , Efficient Diffusion Policies ( Ma et al., 2025 ) , and IDQL ( Hansen-Estruch et al., 2023 ) . A common feature of these methods is that action generation proceeds through a multi-step denoising chain, so inference cost scales with the number of refinement steps. Moreover, existing objectives primarily supervise the terminal denoised action rather than the intermediate prefixes of the chain. As a result, intermediate iterates are generally not trained to be high-value executable decisions. This creates a train–test mismatch whenever inference must be interrupted or truncated under real-time compute constraints. POGP addresses this gap by explicitly assigning value to every prefix of the refinement process through a learned prefix value function thereby turning variable diffusion depth into a first-class object of policy optimization rather than a post hoc deployment heuristic.

sections.heading: Anytime and Adaptive Computation.
sections.text: Our work is also related to the broad area on anytime prediction and adaptive computation. It studies systems whose outputs remain useful when computation is stopped early and improve as additional computation is allocated Zilberstein (1996) ; Graves (2017) ; Huang et al. (2016) ; Banino et al. (2021) . A central challenge in this setting is that models are often optimized only for full-depth performance, which often yields poor intermediate outputs. While exposing the model to variable computation during training, we can improve robustness across budgets and sometimes regularize full-budget performance. POGP brings this perspective into continuous control, where early outputs are not merely intermediate to representations but executable actions whose quality must be judged by downstream return. This distinction is important because unlike adaptive-computation settings in supervised learning, where intermediate predictions are evaluated by task loss. Here, each refinement prefix induces a policy with its own control performance. Our formulation therefore connects adaptive computation to reinforcement learning through value-based supervision over diffusion prefixes.

sections.heading: Efficient and Dynamic Diffusion.
sections.text: Recent efforts to reduce the cost of diffusion inference broadly fall into two categories. The first seeks to improve a predetermined operating point by reducing the number of denoising steps required for good performance. For example through distillation, consistency models or consistency-style policy classes Salimans and Ho (2022) ; Song et al. (2023) ; Ding and Jin (2024) . These approaches substantially reduce latency, but they primarily optimize a chosen small-step generator rather than ensuring that arbitrary prefixes of the original diffusion chain are themselves high-value actions. The second line considers adaptive-budget allocation, where the amount of denoising performed is adjusted online. Most closely related is D3P, which introduces a lightweight adaptor to allocate denoising depth at test time Yu et al. (2025) . POGP differs in both objective and mechanism: instead of learning a separate stopping module, it trains a prefix value function that directly evaluates the marginal utility of further refinement. The same value-grounded object is used both to improve prefix quality during learning and to determine when additional denoising is no longer worthwhile at inference time.

sections.text: A diffusion policy represents π ⁡ ( a ∣ s ) \pi(a\mid s) implicitly via a K K -step reverse denoising chain ( Ho et al., 2020 ; Wang et al., 2022 ) : sample a K ∼ 𝒩 ⁡ ( 0 , I ) a_{K}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I) and apply the denoiser a t − 1 = π θ ( s , a t , t ) , t = K , K − 1 , … , 1 , a_{t-1}\;=\;\pi_{\theta}(s,a_{t},t),\qquad t=K,K-1,\ldots,1, (2) to obtain a 0 a_{0} . In this work, we use a deterministic denoiser (DDIM-style) throughout all experiments. The framework extends to stochastic denoisers by replacing the deterministic refinement transitions with conditional distributions, which we leave as future work.

sections.heading: Prior diffusion RL.
sections.text: Diffusion-QL ( Wang et al., 2022 ) and IDQL ( Hansen-Estruch et al., 2023 ) establish diffusion actors as an expressive policy class in offline (and offline-to-online) RL, while recent on-policy and actor-critic variants scale diffusion policies to fully online training ( Ren et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2024 ; Ding et al., 2024 ) . A shared limitation across these objectives is their terminal-only optimization in which they evaluate the environment through the terminal action a 0 a_{0} . This causes intermediate states to transition in an unsupervised way from noise to the terminal action, but introduce the drawback that internal states are not suitable for direct execution. However, being able to utilize non-complete diffusion chains is critical for dynamic-budget diffusion policies to allow for early stopping of the iterative generation process.

sections.heading: 4 Prefix-Optimal Generative Policies
sections.text: Diffusion policies generate actions through a K K -step denoising chain that transforms random noise into the terminal output action ( a K → ⋯ → a 0 a_{K}\to\cdots\to a_{0} ). Standard training optimizes only the final action a 0 a_{0} , leaving intermediate actions { a t } t = 1 K − 1 \{a_{t}\}_{t=1}^{K-1} without supervision, causing them to be non-executable. a necessary requirement for dynamically choosing the number of refinement steps. POGP addresses this by learning a prefix value function V t ​ ( s , a t ) V_{t}(s,a_{t}) at every denoising step, providing both a training signal that co-trains with the diffusion policy to shape intermediate outputs to be of high quality, as well as a runtime metric that indicates when further denoising is no longer expected to yield significant improvement. Learning the prefix value function requires two core components: 1) a formal definition of prefix values grounded in the environment’s Q-function; and 2) a Bellman-style recursion over the denoising chain that enables efficient TD-based training of V t V_{t} from a single shared chain per gradient step. sections.heading: 4.1 The Prefix Value Function
sections.text: We consider iterative refinement policies defined by a deterministic denoiser π θ \pi_{\theta} : a t − 1 = π θ ( s , a t , t ) , a K ∼ 𝒩 ( 0 , I ) , t = K , … , 1 , a_{t-1}=\pi_{\theta}(s,a_{t},t),\quad a_{K}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I),\quad t=K,\ldots,1, (3) conditioned on environment state s s . To optimize intermediate steps, we require a scalar measure of how “promising” a partial result a t a_{t} is. The natural criterion is the expected return of completing the chain from a t a_{t} : Definition 1 (Prefix Value) . For environment state s s and intermediate action a t a_{t} at refinement step t t : V t π ​ ( s , a t ) := Q π ​ ( s , π full ​ ( s , a t ) ) , V^{\pi}_{t}(s,a_{t})\;:=\;Q^{\pi}\!\bigl(s,\;\pi_{\mathrm{full}}(s,a_{t})\bigr), (4) where π full ​ ( s , a t ) \pi_{\mathrm{full}}(s,a_{t}) denotes the result of running the denoiser from step t t to 0 0 . The prefix value V t V_{t} answers: “If we complete the denoising chain starting from a t a_{t} , what return do we expect?” High V t V_{t} indicates the chain is on track to produce a high- Q Q action; low V t V_{t} signals that continued refinement from a different starting point would have been preferable. Note that for a deterministic denoiser, π full ​ ( s , a t ) = a 0 \pi_{\mathrm{full}}(s,a_{t})=a_{0} for any t t on the same chain, so V t π ​ ( s , a t ) = Q π ​ ( s , a 0 ) V^{\pi}_{t}(s,a_{t})=Q^{\pi}(s,a_{0}) . The value of learning V t V_{t} with a function approximator V ψ ​ ( s , a t , t ) V_{\psi}(s,a_{t},t) is that the network observes only the intermediate action a t a_{t} not the full chain and must therefore learn to predict the quality of the terminal action that would result from completing the chain from a t a_{t} . This enables two capabilities: (1) training the denoiser to maintain high predicted value across all t t and (2) deployment-time monitoring via V ψ V_{\psi} to detect when further refinement yields diminishing returns. Evaluating Eq. ( 4 ) naïvely requires completing the chain ( t t forward passes) for every prefix at every gradient step, multiplying training cost by O ⁡ ( K 2 ) O(K^{2}) . We overcome this by recognizing that refinement possesses temporal structure : V t V_{t} and V t − 1 V_{t-1} are not independent quantities but related through the denoising dynamics. This structure permits efficient credit assignment via dynamic programming.

Larger values of h h place greater weight on the terminal-value anchor, whereas smaller values rely more heavily on the bootstrapped prefix estimate. Unrolling Eq. sections.heading: 5 Experiments
sections.text: We assess POGP on four MuJoCo benchmarks to assess its ability to adapt to the inherent difficulty of different phases of the controlled embodied agent. In particular, we are interested in the following questions: Q1 : Does prefix training improve full-chain performance (see Sec. 5.2 )? Q2 : Can POGP adaptively allocate compute, while retaining performance parity (see Sec. 5.3 )? We further conduct an ablation study to assess the contribution of various components to our method in (see Sec. 5.4 ).

sections.heading: 5.1 Environment and Baseline Configuration
sections.text: Environments. We leverage four distinct environments from the MuJoCo benchmark, namely HalfCheetah-v4, Walker2d-v4, Hopper-v4 and Ant-v4 ( Todorov et al., 2012 ) , spanning action dimensions 3–8. These environments were chosen due to their complexity controlling embodied agents while providing fast simulation as part of the MuJoCo implementation. Baselines. We choose 12 baseline approaches, including TD3 Fujimoto et al. (2018) , SAC Haarnoja et al. (2018) , PPO Schulman et al. (2017) , diffusion policies such as Diffusion-QL Wang et al. (2022) , DPPO Ren et al. (2024) , D 2 PPO Kang et al. (2023) , SDAC Ma et al. (2025) , DSAC-D Liu et al. (2025) and D3P Yu et al. (2025) with D3P being another dynamic diffusion policy. Furthermore, we chose IDQL Hansen-Estruch et al. (2023) as an offline-to-online method as well as generative methods such as FQL Wildberger et al. (2023) and SAC-GMM Nematollahi et al. (2022) . These methods were chosen as recent state-of-the-art methods across a variety of approaches. To ensure a fair comparison, all methods have a similar setup, leveraging a 3-layer MLP with 256 hidden units over a maximum of K = 20 K=20 diffusion steps. During training, we leveraged a batch-size of 256 with a 1M-step replay buffer and 10k steps of exploration. We trained 10 models with different random seeds for our main results and four additional random seeds for the ablation study. All models were trained on a HPC cluster leveraging a single Nvidia A100 GPU for each method, totaling approximately 575 single-GPU hours. Further details about the chosen hyperparameters can be found in Appendix E.2 . Metrics. Each MuJoCo environment provides a dense per-step reward combining a forward-velocity bonus with a control-cost penalty (for Hopper and Walker2d - a survival bonus), so that cumulative episodic return directly measures locomotion quality. We normalise each method’s return to [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] per environment using the range [ random policy , best observed ] [\text{random policy},\text{best observed}] and aggregate across tasks via the interquartile mean (IQM) ( Agarwal et al., 2022 ) , which discards the top and bottom 25% of runs before averaging, yielding a robust summary less sensitive to outlier seeds than the ordinary mean.

sections.heading: 5.2 POGP Baseline Performance on Full Diffusion
sections.text: As our first experiment, we are interested in the performance of POGP as a stand-alone diffusion policy without our proposed PVF-based dynamic diffusion process. Effectively, we assess the performance of POGP with the full K = 20 K=20 diffusion steps, making it equivalent to the other baseline methods tested. Table 1 compares all methods leveraging the maximum allowed number of diffusion steps. We observe that POGP achieves the highest return in all four tested environments. With an average IQM of 0.942 0.942 , providing a 95% CI lower bound (0.908), POGP exceeds every baseline’s point estimate. Three comparisons isolate the gain: POGP vs. SDAC (same backbone): + 9.5 +9.5 on average, POGP vs. SAC-GMM (both multimodal, no chain for MoG): + 34 +34 on HalfCheetah; and POGP vs. D3P : + 5 +5 average. Note that while D3P is a dynamic diffusion model that can stop early, for this test, we enforce all 20 20 diffusion steps (see Table 2 for the dynamic case). Furthermore, in Figure 1 , we show the training curves of the five highest performing baseline methods across the four environments as well as their average IQM performance. In line with the Table 1 results, POGP trains slightly faster than the tested baselines, the IQM profile (rightmost panel) confirms that the gap is consistent across all environments. Together, these results demonstrate that POGP’s prefix-based approach, which optimizes intermediate diffusion steps to provide a high overall value, increases terminal action performance, validating the benefits of the proposed PVF approach. POGP’s improvement is consistent across all four environments.

sections.heading: 6 Discussion
sections.text: POGP shows that optimizing every prefix of a denoising chain yields policies that are both stronger and more compute-efficient. The Prefix Bellman recursion provides credit assignment while the prefix value V ψ V_{\psi} provides the stopping criterion for our dynamic diffusion process. Together, they enable adaptive compute allocation with ∼ 4 {\sim}4 steps for routine states and ∼ 18 {\sim}18 for challenging states (HalfCheetah environment) while retaining most of the model’s overall performance. Our method, POGP, connects to a broader trend of inference time scaling: inference-time compute should be adaptive depending on the difficulty of the desired task. Just as LLM reasoning models learn to “think longer” on hard problems ( Snell et al., 2024 ) , POGP learns to spend more denoising effort on harder states. The key difference is that POGP’s allocation is grounded in a Bellman equation with provable contraction, not heuristic token budgets. The most surprising finding that good intermediate actions also improve the final action suggests the prefix loss acts as an auxiliary regulariser. Limitations. While POGP shows strong results on four MuJoCo benchmarks, additional experiments in robot manipulation tasks are left for future work, introducing a broader complexity divide between different parts of the motion. Furthermore, as POGP’s advantage grows with K K (Appendix I ), scaling to K = 50 + K{=}50{+} chains or real-robot domains remains difficult. Investigating POGP’s ability to scale to large models and long diffusion chains remains an open question. Also see Appendix G for more details on these limitations.

sections.heading: 7 Conclusion
sections.text: In this work, we propose POGP, an approach for learning when to stop computing further denoising iterations in diffusion policies. POGP achieves this by learning a prefix value function (PVF) via a Bellman-style recursion over the denoising chain that serves two purposes: 1) it provides an auxiliary optimization target that shapes intermediate diffusion steps into executable actions, and (2) it offers a test-time stopping criterion that halts denoising when further iterations are not expected to yield meaningful improvement. Across four MuJoCo tasks and 12 baselines, POGP reduces the diffusion compute budget by approximately 66% while retaining near-full performance and outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by approximately 4.6% in aggregate IQM.

sections.heading: Interpretation.
sections.text: The “distill to K ′ = 5 K^{\prime}{=}5 ” row has no retention column because distillation changes the inference protocol: the model is retrained to execute in K ′ K^{\prime} steps, so “truncation” at T = 5 T{=}5 would mean zero refinement, an undefined quantity. The oracle row uses true Q env Q_{\text{env}} values as Hazard TD targets (removing critic approximation error) and serves as an upper bound on what prefix learning alone can achieve with a perfect critic. The two most important ablations are shared chains (S2) and no prefix (baseline). The gap between prefix-supervised and full POGP (4.3 retention points) isolates the contribution of the Hazard Bellman bootstrap specifically, above and beyond any generic intermediate supervision.

sections.heading: D.1 When Does Uniform Training Generalize?
sections.text: Proposition 2 shows that V K ∗ V^{*}_{K} is a convex combination of Q Q -values across all refinement levels, with weights determined by the hazard. A natural question is: for what class of test hazards h test h_{\text{test}} does training under a single hazard h train h_{\text{train}} generalize? Proposition 3 (Generalization via Support Coverage) . If the training hazard h train h_{\text{train}} has h train ​ ( t ) > 0 h_{\text{train}}(t)>0 for all t ∈ { 1 , … , K } t\in\{1,\ldots,K\} , then the fixed point V ∗ V^{*} trained under h train h_{\text{train}} achieves bounded suboptimality under any test hazard h test h_{\text{test}} with h test ​ ( t ) > 0 h_{\text{test}}(t)>0 . Specifically, 𝔼 T ∼ h test ​ [ V ∗ ​ ( s , a T , T ) ] ≥ 𝔼 T ∼ h test ​ [ Q ⁡ ( s , π full ​ ( s , a T ) ) ] − ϵ , \mathbb{E}_{T\sim h_{\text{test}}}[V^{*}(s,a_{T},T)]\;\geq\;\mathbb{E}_{T\sim h_{\text{test}}}[Q(s,\pi_{\text{full}}(s,a_{T}))]\;-\;\epsilon, (30) where ϵ \epsilon depends on the ratio h test ​ ( t ) / h train ​ ( t ) h_{\text{test}}(t)/h_{\text{train}}(t) and the approximation error of V ∗ V^{*} . Under early-biased test hazards (where small T T is likely), the trained policy still performs well because prefixes at all levels were optimized. This theoretical prediction matches the empirical OOD robustness in Table 15 .

sections.heading: E.3 Baseline Implementations
sections.text: All baselines are reimplemented from scratch in the shared codebase to ensure identical data handling, replay buffer management and evaluation protocol. Where baselines have published official code, we verified our implementations match their reported numbers within 2% on a common reference task (HalfCheetah at 1M steps). • TD3 : Twin-delayed DDPG ( Fujimoto et al., 2018 ) . We use the standard hyperparameters and policy smoothing with σ = 0.2 \sigma{=}0.2 , clip c = 0.5 c{=}0.5 . • SAC : Soft actor-critic ( Haarnoja et al., 2018 ) with automatic entropy tuning. • PPO : Proximal policy optimization ( Schulman et al., 2017 ) with 64 parallel environments, clip ϵ = 0.2 \epsilon{=}0.2 , 10 epochs per update. • Diffusion-QL : Diffusion policy with Q Q -weighted behavioral cloning loss ( Wang et al., 2022 ) . Online variant with no offline pretraining. • DPPO / D 2 PPO : Diffusion policy optimized with PPO-style updates ( Ren et al., 2024 ) . D 2 PPO adds a second denoising stage. • SDAC : Score-matching diffusion actor-critic ( Ma et al., 2025 ) . Uses a score-matching auxiliary loss to avoid backpropagating through the full chain. • DSAC-D : Liu et al. (2025) Diffusion extension of soft actor-critic with direct score-based policy updates. • D3P : Yu et al. (2025) Diffusion policy with a learned depth-selection prior and dynamic early exit. • IDQL : Offline implicit diffusion Q Q -learning ( Hansen-Estruch et al., 2023 ) with 100K offline pre-training steps from a random-policy replay buffer, followed by 900K online fine-tuning. • FQL : Flow Q Q -learning ( Wildberger et al., 2023 ) ; the flow-based policy is trained with a reflow objective to enable one-step action generation. • SAC-GMM : SAC Nematollahi et al. (2022) with a 5-component Gaussian mixture policy. Serves as a capacity-matched multimodal baseline without iterative refinement.

sections.heading: Appendix I Chain Length Sensitivity
sections.text: A key question is how POGP’s advantage scales with the denoising chain length K K . Longer chains increase the cost of full inference and amplify the benefit of early stopping, but also make prefix training harder (more levels to optimize). We evaluate K ∈ { 5 , 10 , 15 , 20 } K\in\{5,10,15,20\} across all four environments.

I.2 Discussion
sections.text: Three trends emerge from Table 14 : 1. POGP’s retention advantage grows with K K . At K = 5 K{=}5 , the retention gap over SDAC is modest ( ∼ \sim 2–3 percentage points) because short chains leave little room for truncation degradation. By K = 20 K{=}20 , the gap widens to ∼ \sim 15–17 points: SDAC’s retention drops steadily as the chain lengthens, while POGP maintains > > 97% retention at half-chain truncation across all environments. 2. Full-chain return improves monotonically with K K for both methods. Longer chains provide more expressive policies. POGP consistently outperforms SDAC in absolute return at every K K , with a roughly constant gap of ∼ \sim 28–30 points on HalfCheetah. The prefix training objective does not harm full-chain quality. 3. POGP’s retention is approximately constant across K K . While SDAC’s retention at half-chain drops from ∼ \sim 96% ( K = 5 K{=}5 ) to ∼ \sim 82% ( K = 20 K{=}20 ), POGP’s retention stays in the narrow band of 97–99% regardless of chain length. This confirms that the Hazard Bellman operator successfully propagates prefix value information across arbitrarily many refinement levels, as predicted by the contraction analysis (Theorem 1). These results suggest that POGP becomes increasingly valuable as diffusion-policy practitioners adopt longer chains for more complex tasks. Whether this scaling extends beyond K = 20 K{=}20 to the very long chains used in image generation ( K = 50 K{=}50 – 100 100 ) remains an open question; we anticipate that architectural modifications to the prefix critic (e.g., attention over refinement levels) may be needed to maintain stable backward induction over such depths.

sections.heading: M.1 Diffusion Models for Offline RL and Planning
sections.text: The use of diffusion models in RL predates online training formulations. Janner et al. (2022) use diffusion to model entire trajectory distributions, enabling planning by sampling and reranking trajectories. Wang et al. (2022) introduce Diffusion-QL, the first to use a diffusion actor with Q Q -weighted fine-tuning in offline settings. These offline methods implicitly assume inference always completes; POGP’s prefix training extends their objectives to the online, variable-compute setting.

sections.heading: M.2 Relationship to Progressive Training
sections.text: Progressive distillation ( Salimans and Ho, 2022 ) and consistency models ( Song et al., 2023 ) train models to match the output of many-step samplers with fewer steps. While both improve efficiency, they optimize for a fixed reduced K K rather than arbitrary truncation depths. POGP is complementary: one could apply progressive distillation to reduce K K from 20 to 10, then apply POGP to make the K = 20 K{=}20 chain truncation-robust.

sections.heading: M.3 Relationship to Options and Temporal Abstraction
sections.text: The options framework ( Sutton et al., 1999 ) decomposes environment-time policies into temporally extended behaviors with initiation conditions and termination functions. POGP’s refinement MDP shares the termination-over-time structure, but operates in refinement time rather than environment time. A formal unification where an option’s internal computation is itself a prefix-optimal process could extend POGP to hierarchical settings.

sections.heading: M.4 Relationship to Adaptive Computation Time
sections.text: ACT ( Graves, 2017 ) and PonderNet ( Banino et al., 2021 ) learn when to halt iterative computation in supervised settings. POGP provides the RL analogue: the stopping rule emerges naturally from the learned prefix value V ψ V_{\psi} , without a separate halting network. Unlike ACT, POGP’s stopping criterion is grounded in expected return rather than a cost penalizing computation.

sections.heading: Positive impact.
sections.text: POGP reduces the compute required for diffusion-policy inference in robotics and continuous control: 2 2 – 4 × 4\times speedups with < < 5% quality loss translate directly into lower energy consumption and faster control loops. In safety-critical settings (e.g., prosthetics, industrial robots), the anytime guarantee that interruption yields a usable action is a meaningful safety property.

sections.heading: Limitations.
sections.text: 1. Evaluation scope. Results are limited to MuJoCo locomotion. Whether prefix training generalizes to manipulation, navigation, or real-robot settings is unknown. 2. Stochastic denoisers. The main text uses deterministic DDIM-style denoisers. Stochastic denoisers require modifying the refinement MDP to include stochastic transitions; the Hazard Bellman operator extends, but contraction rate analysis would need to account for transition noise. 3. Long chains. The advantage of POGP over SDAC grows with K K (Appendix I ), but experiments are limited to K ≤ 20 K\leq 20 . Whether this continues to K = 50 K{=}50 or K = 100 K{=}100 (as used in image generation) is unexplored and may require architectural changes to the prefix critic. 4. Seed sensitivity. One in four evaluated seeds (seed 100) failed to benefit from prefix training due to late gate opening. A more robust gating criterion is needed for reliable deployment.

We introduce POGP, which learns a prefix value function at every denoising step through a Bellman-style recursion. The prefix value function improves intermediate action quality and provides a test-time signal for adaptive stopping. Across four MuJoCo environments and 12 baselines, POGP outperforms D3P by approximately 3.5% while using 18.2% fewer iterations. Relative to a fixed 20-step chain, POGP reduces denoising computation by approximately 2.7 × 2.7\times while retaining near-full-chain performance. Contribution(s) 1. Prefix Value Function: A value function trained via TD bootstrapping over the denoising chain that serves as an auxiliary objective improving intermediate action quality. Context: Diffusion policies optimize only the terminal action, leaving intermediate iterates unsupervised and non-executable. 2. Learned Early Stopping: A stopping rule requiring no separately learned halting network derived from consecutive prefix value differences that halts denoising when further refinement is predicted to yield negligible improvement. Context: Prior acceleration methods either apply fixed step reductions or train separate adapter networks decoupled from intermediate action quality. 3. Empirical Validation: Prefix training improves full-chain performance by approximately 4.6% over state-of-the-art baselines while enabling ≈ 2.7 × \approx 2.7\times compute savings across four MuJoCo environments and 12 baselines. Context: The dual benefit suggests intermediate supervision acts as a beneficial auxiliary objective beyond enabling adaptive compute allocation. Abstract Diffusion policies have emerged as a powerful policy class for continuous control, but their iterative denoising process remains the primary computational bottleneck. Optimizing the computational effort spent per action is critical for improving the practical adoption of diffusion policies, allowing them to allocate more iterations only when the task demands it. To this end, we propose POGP (Prefix-Optimal Generative Policies), which learns a prefix value function (PVF) at every intermediate denoising step via a Bellman-style recursion over the chain. The PVF provides both an auxiliary optimization target that shapes intermediate outputs into high-quality actions and a test-time stopping criterion that halts denoising when further iterations are not expected to yield meaningful improvement. Through extensive experiments on four MuJoCo environments against 12 baselines, we demonstrate that POGP reduces the required denoising iterations by approximately 2.7 × 2.7\times while retaining near-full performance. Furthermore, compared to current state-of-the-art dynamic diffusion baselines, we show that prefix training improves final task performance by approximately 3.5%, suggesting that supervising intermediate denoising steps acts as a beneficial auxiliary objective beyond its role in enabling early stopping. Project Page : https://rohitsalla.github.io/POGP 1 Introduction Diffusion policies for continuous control generate actions through an iterative denoising chain, typically requiring K K sequential neural network evaluations per action ( Ho et al., 2020 ; Chi et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2022 ) . Running all K K iterations of the diffusion process is the primary computational bottleneck of diffusion policies as every action incurs the same computational cost regardless of the task’s difficulty. In practice, however, many actions taken by an embodied system along some trajectory are routine and well-determined after only a few denoising steps, while others, such as contact-rich transitions, disturbance recovery, or mode switches strongly benefit from extended refinement steps. For example, consider an embodied agent perturbed by some external force. When the disturbance is applied to the system, the policy benefits from additional refinement steps to improve the system’s overall behavior while saving compute at other times, which is especially important for local and edge deployments on real robot hardware. Current diffusion policy frameworks ( Ren et al., 2024 ; Ma et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2024 ; Hansen-Estruch et al., 2023 ) do not distinguish between these cases, spending compute uniformly across the trajectory. Recent approaches leveraging diffusion policies ( Yu et al., 2025 ) address this issue by estimating the number of iterations needed in order to reach a sufficiently performant action. However, because this adapter is independent of the policy, the intermediate denoising steps are never optimized to be executable as the model is only trained on the full diffusion process. We take a different approach by jointly training a prefix value function (PVF) alongside the diffusion policy itself, which both improves intermediate action quality as an auxiliary objective and provides a natural per-step stopping signal at test time. In this work, we propose a novel approach for dynamic diffusion – Prefix-Optimal Generative Policies (POGP) – that leverages a learned prefix value function (PVF) to assess when diffusion iterations can be stopped early while improving the quality of internal diffusion iterations . POGP trains a PVF V t ​ ( s , a t ) V_{t}(s,a_{t}) for each intermediate action a t a_{t} in the K K -step diffusion chain a K → a 0 a_{K}\to a_{0} that intuitively measures how valuable it would be to execute action a t a_{t} at step t t . During training, the PVF is trained to estimate an action’s value by completing all K K diffusion steps, co-evolving as an optimization target for the diffusion step itself. Crucially, rather than regressing each V t V_{t} independently against the final action’s Q-value, which would require expensive full-chain rollouts per step, we derive a Bellman recursion over the denoising chain that propagates value information backwards through refinement steps, enabling efficient single-chain training with stable TD targets. Intuitively, the PVF serves a dual purpose: 1) it improves the quality of the intermediate policy actions a t a_{t} ; and 2) provides a metric for stopping the diffusion process early in order to save time and compute budget. We demonstrate that, across four MuJoCo tasks and 12 baselines, POGP achieves an IQM of 0.942 0.942 with a 95 % 95\% confidence interval ( Agarwal et al., 2022 ) , retains ≥ 97.8 % \geq 97.8\% of its full-diffusion process task performance at less than half the computation cost and outperforms current state-of-the-art baselines by ≈ 4.6 % \approx 4.6\% . In summary, POGP proposes the following contributions: • a prefix value function trained via TD bootstrapping alongside the diffusion model over the denoising chain, ultimately improving the quality of the intermediate steps; • a principled early stopping rule derived from prefix value differences across consecutive diffusion steps, leveraged to stop the diffusion policy early if the value of future steps is predicted to be minimal; and • empirical evidence that prefix training improves full-chain performance by up to 4.6 % 4.6\% while enabling ≈ 2.7 × \approx 2.7\times compute savings, on average. 2 Related Work Diffusion Policies for Control. Diffusion-based policies have emerged as a powerful class of decision models for continuous control and robot learning because they can represent complex, multimodal action distributions that are difficult for unimodal actors to capture. Prior work includes action-diffusion policies for manipulation ( Chi et al., 2024 ) , diffusion-based trajectory planning ( Janner et al., 2022 ) , and diffusion-parameterized reinforcement learning methods such as Diffusion-QL ( Wang et al., 2022 ) , Efficient Diffusion Policies ( Ma et al., 2025 ) , and IDQL ( Hansen-Estruch et al., 2023 ) . A common feature of these methods is that action generation proceeds through a multi-step denoising chain, so inference cost scales with the number of refinement steps. Moreover, existing objectives primarily supervise the terminal denoised action rather than the intermediate prefixes of the chain. As a result, intermediate iterates are generally not trained to be high-value executable decisions. This creates a train–test mismatch whenever inference must be interrupted or truncated under real-time compute constraints. POGP addresses this gap by explicitly assigning value to every prefix of the refinement process through a learned prefix value function thereby turning variable diffusion depth into a first-class object of policy optimization rather than a post hoc deployment heuristic. Anytime and Adaptive Computation. Our work is also related to the broad area on anytime prediction and adaptive computation. It studies systems whose outputs remain useful when computation is stopped early and improve as additional computation is allocated Zilberstein (1996) ; Graves (2017) ; Huang et al. (2016) ; Banino et al. (2021) . A central challenge in this setting is that models are often optimized only for full-depth performance, which often yields poor intermediate outputs. While exposing the model to variable computation during training, we can improve robustness across budgets and sometimes regularize full-budget performance. POGP brings this perspective into continuous control, where early outputs are not merely intermediate to representations but executable actions whose quality must be judged by downstream return. This distinction is important because unlike adaptive-computation settings in supervised learning, where intermediate predictions are evaluated by task loss. Here, each refinement prefix induces a policy with its own control performance. Our formulation therefore connects adaptive computation to reinforcement learning through value-based supervision over diffusion prefixes. Efficient and Dynamic Diffusion. Recent efforts to reduce the cost of diffusion inference broadly fall into two categories. The first seeks to improve a predetermined operating point by reducing the number of denoising steps required for good performance. For example through distillation, consistency models or consistency-style policy classes Salimans and Ho (2022) ; Song et al. (2023) ; Ding and Jin (2024) . These approaches substantially reduce latency, but they primarily optimize a chosen small-step generator rather than ensuring that arbitrary prefixes of the original diffusion chain are themselves high-value actions. The second line considers adaptive-budget allocation, where the amount of denoising performed is adjusted online. Most closely related is D3P, which introduces a lightweight adaptor to allocate denoising depth at test time Yu et al. (2025) . POGP differs in both objective and mechanism: instead of learning a separate stopping module, it trains a prefix value function that directly evaluates the marginal utility of further refinement. The same value-grounded object is used both to improve prefix quality during learning and to determine when additional denoising is no longer worthwhile at inference time. 3 Background and Notation Notation We summarize key notation as follows: s ∈ 𝒮 s\in\mathcal{S} and a t ∈ 𝒜 a_{t}\in\mathcal{A} represent the environment state and action at refinement level t t , respectively, where t ∈ { 0 , … , K } t\in\{0,\ldots,K\} runs backwards ( t = K t{=}K is noise, t = 0 t{=}0 is the terminal action). We leverage four distinct environments from the MuJoCo benchmark, namely HalfCheetah-v4, Walker2d-v4, Hopper-v4 and Ant-v4 ( Todorov et al., 2012 ) , spanning action dimensions 3–8. These environments were chosen due to their complexity controlling embodied agents while providing fast simulation as part of the MuJoCo implementation. Baselines. We choose 12 baseline approaches, including TD3 Fujimoto et al. (2018) , SAC Haarnoja et al. (2018) , PPO Schulman et al. (2017) , diffusion policies such as Diffusion-QL Wang et al. (2022) , DPPO Ren et al. (2024) , D 2 PPO Kang et al. (2023) , SDAC Ma et al. (2025) , DSAC-D Liu et al. (2025) and D3P Yu et al. (2025) with D3P being another dynamic diffusion policy. Furthermore, we chose IDQL Hansen-Estruch et al. (2023) as an offline-to-online method as well as generative methods such as FQL Wildberger et al. (2023) and SAC-GMM Nematollahi et al. (2022) . These methods were chosen as recent state-of-the-art methods across a variety of approaches. To ensure a fair comparison, all methods have a similar setup, leveraging a 3-layer MLP with 256 hidden units over a maximum of K = 20 K=20 diffusion steps. During training, we leveraged a batch-size of 256 with a 1M-step replay buffer and 10k steps of exploration. We trained 10 models with different random seeds for our main results and four additional random seeds for the ablation study. All models were trained on a HPC cluster leveraging a single Nvidia A100 GPU for each method, totaling approximately 575 single-GPU hours. Further details about the chosen hyperparameters can be found in Appendix E.2 . Metrics. Each MuJoCo environment provides a dense per-step reward combining a forward-velocity bonus with a control-cost penalty (for Hopper and Walker2d - a survival bonus), so that cumulative episodic return directly measures locomotion quality.
